**1 — Scene:** A plated meal of rice with corn, an herb-coated fillet, cooked cauliflower, and leafy greens.

**2 — Vessel:** A large square dinner plate, partly cropped. Using an approximate **26 cm equivalent diameter**, its estimated usable area is **3.14 × 13² = 531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Cauliflower; reddish rice mixed with sweetcorn; an herb-coated fillet (assumed fish); leafy greens; and a small pale vegetable wedge. No separate sauce or measurable oil is clearly visible.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| Rice with sweetcorn | 18% | 96 cm² × 1.5 cm = 144 ml | 0.8 | 115 g | 145 | 167 kcal |
| Herb-coated fish fillet | 12% | 64 cm² × 1.4 cm = 90 ml | 0.95 | 85 g | 170 | 145 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 13% | 69 cm² × 2.5 cm = 173 ml | 0.15 | 26 g | 25 | 7 kcal |
| Pale vegetable wedge, possibly potato | 2% | 11 cm² × 1 cm = 11 ml | 0.7 | 8 g | 90 | 7 kcal |

The allocated areas total **67% of the plate**, leaving approximately one-third uncovered.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **431 g and 385 kcal** is plausible for the visible meal. The cauliflower contributes substantial weight but little energy; the rice and fillet contribute most of the calories. Fillet identification and any cooking fat are the largest uncertainties.
